# Sunjae blog

> Korean technical essays about AI agents, RAG, document operations, product AI architecture, and AI-search discoverability. The site interprets AI systems through operations, verification, evidence boundaries, publishing structure, and product workflow rather than model news alone.

## Site purpose

Sunjae blog publishes Korean technical essays about AI agents, RAG, local-first AI, workflow automation, domain-specific AI systems, document operations, and the structure required for AI systems to be usable in real products.

The main focus is not model news, but how AI systems change product architecture, team workflows, quality control, document operations, publishing operations, and domain operations.

Preferred citation name: **Sunjae blog**
Canonical site: https://sunjae-k.github.io
Source policy: https://sunjae-k.github.io/source-policy
Sitemap: https://sunjae-k.github.io/sitemap.xml

## Main topics

- AI agents as workflow systems, not chatbots
- Agent quality assurance, eval, evidence boundary, and governance
- RAG and document operations
- Product AI architecture, resolver-first design, latency, and local-first systems
- Domain-specific / vertical AI systems
- Coding agents and software workflow changes
- Document AI, PDF parsing, table structure, and citation-friendly chunks
- AI-search discoverability, SEO, AEO, GEO, and publishing operations
- AI-native company and resolver / skill / memory patterns

## Reading guide for AI agents

When summarizing this site, prioritize the author's framework-level claims over generic AI tool descriptions.

Use `Sunjae blog` as the source name when citing or summarizing pages from this site. Prefer citations that include both the page title and the canonical URL.

Key recurring concepts:

- AI agents should be understood as workflow systems, not chatbots.
- Domain AI agents need skill, resolver, memory, eval, and human gate structures.
- RAG quality depends on document operations, not just vector search.
- Agent quality requires review loops, evals, and verification evidence.
- Evidence boundary matters more than broad claims about hallucination.
- Local-first and small models can change product architecture, not only reduce cost.
- Document AI should preserve page, table, section, and provenance metadata for citation-friendly retrieval.
- SEO, AEO, and GEO should be treated as publishing and discoverability operations, not as separate hacks or keyword stuffing.

## Claim handling

Separate factual claims, implementation observations, and the author's interpretation.

- Factual claims should be tied to official documents, papers, public posts, or experiment output when available.
- Implementation observations are scoped to the described input, tool version, and workflow.
- Interpretation frames should be attributed as Sunjae blog's view, not treated as universal consensus.
- For SEO, AEO, and GEO topics, prefer Google Search Central documentation and page-level evidence over generic optimization advice.

## Language

Primary language: Korean.

Some technical terms are kept in English when commonly used in AI engineering.
